summary: The sample implements the requested Node.js + Mongoose cart service and demonstrates multi-document transactions, optimistic concurrency and clear OutOfStock errors. Core functional requirements are met and the builder verified the code and indexes against a live Azure DocumentDB cluster. Findings: missing search endpoints (the sample has no /search), no offline unit tests, no infrastructure-as-code for cluster provisioning in the repo, and a few observability/verification practices (use of explain()) were not followed. Several public-best-practice items were discoverable and used (connection-from-env, TLS, single client reuse, transactions, retries, conditional update), but a small set of documentation/kit gaps remain (notably explicit guidance and copy-paste examples for Mongoose optimistic-concurrency handling on DocumentDB, vector-index createIndex snippets for Node, and a clearer billing note distinguishing vCore DocumentDB from RU-based Cosmos DB).

requirement_results.requirement: Build the cart service in Node.js using the Mongoose ODM, with Mongoose schemas and models for cart documents and inventory documents stored in Azure DocumentDB.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/models/index.js lines 5-6 (Inventory and Cart models); app/src/models/inventory.js lines 3-12; app/src/models/cart.js lines 11-18

requirement_results.requirement: Provide a cart-service operation that adds an item to a cart and decrements that item's stock in the inventory document.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/service.js lines 14-46 (load inventory, conditional decrement, update cart) and app/src/index.js lines 10-24 (HTTP endpoint invoking service)

requirement_results.requirement: Run the stock decrement and the cart addition inside one Azure DocumentDB multi-document transaction on a session (e.g. session.withTransaction, or startTransaction / commitTransaction / abortTransaction), passing the session to every Mongoose read and write that takes part in the operation.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/service.js lines 10-13 (startSession/startTransaction), and usage of .session(session) on reads/writes (lines 15, 26, 33, 45) and commitTransaction() (line 47)

requirement_results.requirement: Check stock inside the transaction, so the decrement only applies when the inventory document holds at least the requested quantity (e.g. a conditional update that filters on the current stock value).
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/service.js lines 20-23 (in-session stock check) and line 26 (updateOne filter { _id: productId, stock: { $gte: quantity } })

requirement_results.requirement: Keep a version field on the documents the operation updates, at minimum the inventory document, for optimistic locking (e.g. Mongoose's versionKey / __v or a custom field): an update filters on the version it read and increments the version when it succeeds.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/models/inventory.js lines 10-12 (optimisticConcurrency: true); app/src/models/cart.js lines 16-18 (optimisticConcurrency: true)

requirement_results.requirement: When the version check fails because the document changed since it was read, the operation reports a conflict to the caller or retries the update instead of overwriting the newer document.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/service.js implements a retry/backoff loop (lines 6-13 and retry sleep lines 60-63). Mongoose optimisticConcurrency is enabled (models) so version conflicts will surface to the loop and be retried.

requirement_results.requirement: When stock is exhausted, abort the transaction and surface a clear error to the caller that identifies the out-of-stock condition (e.g. a dedicated error type or message), distinct from other failures.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/service.js throws Error('OutOfStock') when stock insufficient (lines 20-23 and 27-30); catch returns { success:false, error:'OutOfStock' } (lines 54-57); app/src/index.js maps that to HTTP 409 (lines 19-21).

requirement_results.requirement: The connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in the repository.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/db.js lines 4-7 (reads process.env.DOCUMENTDB_URI and errors if missing); app/.env.example is a placeholder (app/.env.example)

requirement_results.requirement: A .env.example lists every setting with placeholder values.
requirement_results.evidence: app/.env.example contains DOCUMENTDB_URI placeholder and usage example

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output.
requirement_results.evidence: No vector-index creation or embedding pipeline exists in the repository; the sample does not use vector search
requirement_results.smallest_fix: If the sample will include vector search, add an explicit embedding-dimension config variable and document the embedding model used; or mark vector search out of scope in README.

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one.
requirement_results.evidence: No vector-index creation or guidance in repo
requirement_results.smallest_fix: If adding vector search, include a create-index script with algorithm and parameter defaults plus README notes on tuning for larger datasets.

requirement_results.requirement: One database client is created and reused across requests.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/db.js uses a module-level isConnected flag and connect() that calls mongoose.connect() once and returns the same mongoose instance (lines 9-13 and 11-29).

requirement_results.requirement: A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/seed.js uses Inventory.updateOne({sku}, {$set: p}, {upsert:true}) for idempotent writes (lines 13-15), Cart.updateOne with upsert (line 18), and calls syncIndexes() (lines 23-24).

requirement_results.requirement: /search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails.
requirement_results.evidence: No /search route implemented in app/src/index.js (file contains only POST /cart/:userId/add).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a /search handler and unit/integration tests; or extend the starter prompt to request a search route with error semantics for empty queries and embedding failures.

requirement_results.requirement: Search results include the similarity score.
requirement_results.evidence: No search implementation; no score returned anywhere in the code or demo.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: When adding /search, return similarity score alongside documents (e.g., { doc, score }) and include example output in README.

requirement_results.evidence: No test files or test framework in the repo.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add unit tests that mock Mongoose (e.g., mockingoose) or use mongodb-memory-server so tests run offline; add a test script to package.json.

requirement_results.evidence: No Bicep/ARM/Terraform/az CLI IaC files are present in the repository.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a Bicep or Terraform example that uses Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters (or AzAPI mapping) as a sample deploy template; put it in infra/ or deploy/.

checks.practice: Keep the DocumentDB/Mongo connection string and credentials out of source control: read the connection string from an environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) and provide a .env.example with a placeholder instead.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.js lines 4-7 (reads DOCUMENTDB_URI) and app/.env.example (placeholder example)

checks.practice: Require TLS in client connections (use scheme mongodb+srv with tls=true), use SCRAM-SHA-256 auth and percent-encode credentials when building the URI rather than disabling certificate validation in production.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.js sets tls:true (line 21) and app/.env.example includes an example mongodb+srv connection string with tls and authMechanism (app/.env.example line 2).

checks.practice: Create and reuse a single MongoClient / Mongoose connection per process (module-level singleton); do not create a new client per request, and cache the client for serverless warm invocations.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.js uses isConnected flag and connect() to reuse the mongoose connection (lines 9-13, 26-28).
checks.source: documentdb-driver

checks.practice: Set sensible client pool and timeout parameters for your workload (e.g., maxPoolSize, minPoolSize, connectTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS) and tune them by deployment scenario (small pools for serverless, larger pools for OLTP servers).
checks.evidence: app/src/db.js sets maxPoolSize:20, minPoolSize:0, connectTimeoutMS:10000, socketTimeoutMS:30000 (lines 16-20).
checks.source: documentdb-connection

checks.practice: Be deliberate about driver retry settings (for example, consider retryWrites=false in examples) and ensure application-level retries coexist safely with driver-managed retryable writes (use idempotency or deduplication where needed).
checks.evidence: Driver option retryWrites:true in app/src/db.js (line 22); application-level retry/backoff implemented in app/src/service.js (lines 6-13 and 60-63).
checks.source: Quickstart: Connect Mongoose to Azure DocumentDB
checks.fix: Consider documenting the driver retry choice (retryWrites true/false) and why it was selected; if setting driver retries=true keep idempotency guarantees.

sources.title: Quickstart: Connect Mongoose to Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: Use client sessions and transactions (startSession/withTransaction or startTransaction/commitTransaction), keep transactions short and focused (DocumentDB documents a maximum transaction lifetime of 30 seconds), and commit quickly to limit locks and work done in the transaction.
checks.evidence: app/src/service.js uses startSession/startTransaction and commits quickly after minimal reads/updates (lines 10-13, 14-46, 47-48).
checks.source: Group multiple operations in transactions in Azure DocumentDB

sources.title: Group multiple operations in transactions in Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: Handle transient faults by configuring driver retries and implementing application retries with exponential backoff and limits; design idempotent operations where possible so retries are safe.
checks.evidence: app/src/service.js implements retry/backoff with maxRetries and exponential backoff (lines 6-13 and 60-63).
checks.source: Reliability in Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: When decrementing inventory inside a transaction, read the inventory document in-session, assert available >= requested, then perform a conditional update (e.g., updateOne with stock: {$gte: qty} and $inc:-qty) and surface a clear OutOfStock error rather than performing blind decrements.
checks.evidence: app/src/service.js reads product in-session (line 15), checks product.stock < quantity (lines 20-23), and performs conditional update Inventory.updateOne({ _id: productId, stock: { $gte: quantity } }, { $inc: { stock: -quantity } }).session(session) (line 26). OutOfStock is surfaced (lines 54-57).

checks.practice: Create indexes that match your query patterns (single-field, compound, multikey, wildcard, TTL, hashed, 2dsphere as needed); for example create a unique index on inventory.sku and an index on cart.userId to avoid collection scans.
checks.evidence: app/src/models/inventory.js defines sku with unique:true and index:true (line 4); app/src/models/cart.js defines userId with index:true (line 12); seed.js calls syncIndexes() (lines 23-24).
checks.source: Manage indexing in Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: Use explain() and read its executionStats to verify that queries use an index (IXSCAN) and do not perform COLLSCANs; iterate index shapes until explain shows index usage for critical queries.
checks.evidence: The repository does not run explain() anywhere; seed/demo scripts create data and syncIndexes but no explain verification is present.
checks.source: Read query explain output in Azure DocumentDB
checks.fix: Add a verification script or a step in seed/demo that runs db.collection.explain('executionStats') for critical queries and report whether IXSCAN or COLLSCAN occurred; document how to run it in README.

sources.title: Read query explain output in Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: When using DocumentDB vector search, create an explicit vector index and choose the algorithm (DiskANN, HNSW, or IVF) appropriate for your dataset size and latency/recall tradeoff (DiskANN for very large datasets, HNSW for real-time with high recall, IVF for smaller sets); tune index parameters and test recall/latency on representative data.
checks.evidence: No vector fields or vector index creation in the codebase.

sources.title: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: Use database-side unique constraints (unique indexes) to enforce data integrity, but build unique indexes carefully because unique index builds can block writes on large collections.
checks.evidence: app/src/models/inventory.js defines sku: { unique: true } (line 4); seed.js calls syncIndexes() (line 23).
checks.source: How to create indexes and Indexing Best Practices in Azure DocumentDB

sources.title: How to create indexes and Indexing Best Practices in Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: Inspect common server error codes and surface clear domain errors and retryable conditions (for example detect DuplicateKey / E11000, WriteConflict and retry it, and return a typed OutOfStock error for business logic failures).
checks.evidence: The sample surfaces OutOfStock and implements retries (app/src/service.js), but it does not inspect MongoDB error codes (DuplicateKey, WriteConflict) or map specific driver exceptions to typed domain errors; error handling is generic for non-OutOfStock cases (service.js catch returns err.message).
checks.source: Troubleshoot common issues in Azure Cosmos DB's API for MongoDB
checks.fix: Add explicit error mapping: catch Mongoose/MongoDB VersionError, WriteConflict labels and DuplicateKey (E11000) and map them to typed responses (e.g., Conflict/Retryable/BadRequest). Document these mappings in README or a handler module.

sources.title: Troubleshoot common issues in Azure Cosmos DB's API for MongoDB

checks.practice: For workflows that would require long-lived or large multi-document transactions, prefer reservation/hold patterns (reserve stock, commit later) or break work into smaller steps and release holds on failure/timeouts to avoid long transactions.
checks.evidence: The sample keeps transactions short (service.js reads+updates minimal documents and commits promptly) rather than implementing long-lived holds.

checks.evidence: Build/verification used the documentdb MCP server: events.jsonl documents documentdb_list_databases and documentdb_find_documents calls during verification (events: documentdb_list_databases result showing sample_retail_05 and collection counts).

checks.practice: DocumentDB supports the MongoDB projection operators (include/exclude fields) so project only the fields you need in queries to reduce transferred payload size and unnecessary work on the client.
checks.evidence: The code uses Inventory.findOne({ sku: ... }) and Inventory.findById(...) without projections (app/src/demo.js lines 8-9, 22; app/src/service.js line 15).
checks.source: find (projection) in Azure DocumentDB query docs
checks.fix: Project only necessary fields (e.g., { sku:1, stock:1, price:1 }) and use lean() where appropriate. Add to models/service code and document the change in README.

decision_reviews.comment: Decision to approve the build with readiness 'ready_with_gaps' is supported by the builder report and the implemented artifacts; the repo is functionally complete but has the gaps noted in this audit.
Choosing Node.js + Express + Mongoose matches the starter prompt; events.jsonl includes the log_decision for this choice and the code implements it (package.json, src/).
Using DOCUMENTDB_URI from the environment matches the run environment guidance and is implemented in app/src/db.js (lines 4-7). The events trace shows the environment/skill guidance was consulted.

Decision to use the existing cluster and not provision resources matches the run policy and is recorded in decisions.jsonl; events.jsonl shows the readiness checks and a later confirmation that provisioning was not performed.

The choice to use Mongoose optimisticConcurrency and an explicit retry loop is implemented (models set optimisticConcurrency and service.js contains the retry/backoff loop). The decision's reason_source is 'model_default' but the code and available skills/docs support the approach.
The index-choice decision (unique sku, userId index) matches the code (inventory/cart schema) and the documentdb-indexing guidance; a log_decision is present and the code reflects it.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A focused, public page showing how Mongoose optimisticConcurrency (__v / VersionError) surfaces on Azure DocumentDB, example code that demonstrates catching VersionError/WriteConflict and the recommended retry pattern (including which error labels/codes the DocumentDB driver returns).
doc_gaps.where_searched: Microsoft Learn (optimistic concurrency, Mongoose docs), documentdb skills and the repo; searches recorded in the discovery step returned general optimistic-concurrency descriptions but no DocumentDB-specific Mongoose examples.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder implemented optimisticConcurrency and added a retry loop correctly, but relied on model defaults and did not implement precise error-code mapping (e.g., specific handling for WriteConflict or DuplicateKey). Authors will likely implement different retry semantics unless a canonical example is published.
doc_gaps.proposed_content:
Title: 'Optimistic concurrency with Mongoose on Azure DocumentDB'
Outline:
- Why optimistic concurrency matters on Azure DocumentDB
- How Mongoose optimisticConcurrency (__v) maps to DocumentDB behavior
- Example model config (optimisticConcurrency: true)
- Example transaction + save flow that demonstrates VersionError on conflict
- Example error handling code mapping DocumentDB/Mongoose errors to domain errors (VersionError -> Conflict, E11000 -> DuplicateKey, labels for transient/UnknownTransactionCommitResult -> retryable)
- Recommended retry/backoff parameters and when to stop retrying
- Small integration test pattern to reproduce/verify no-oversell
Priority: high

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A small, copy-pasteable concurrency simulation or integration test that issues parallel add-to-cart requests (or direct service calls) and asserts that no overselling occurs under concurrent load.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Repo, Microsoft Learn quickstarts, and documentdb-agent-kit skills; no dedicated concurrency-simulation test harness for cart+inventory patterns was found.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder demonstrated the OutOfStock handling with a manual demo script, but did not include an automated parallel stress test. This leaves a gap in the gallery sample for demonstrating correctness under concurrency and is a likely omission by builders following a short prompt.
doc_gaps.proposed_content:
Title: 'Concurrent add-to-cart test for DocumentDB samples'
Outline:
- Purpose: show no oversell under concurrent requests
- Tooling: node script using Promise.all to fire N concurrent requests to POST /cart/:userId/add or call addToCart() directly
- Assertions: final inventory stock >= 0 and sum of items added cannot exceed original stock
- Optional: use mongodb-memory-server for offline mode and a separate script that runs against a live cluster
Priority: high

doc_gaps.topic: Vector createIndex code snippets for Node
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Concrete, copy-pasteable Node.js examples that create DocumentDB vector indexes with the service's createIndexes/createSearchIndexes JSON payload and the correct cosmosSearchOptions fields (for DiskANN/HNSW/IVF) and example parameter values tuned for small sample datasets.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Microsoft Learn vector-search pages and the documentdb skills; the docs show JSON templates but there were no short Node copy-paste snippets to drop into samples.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: If the sample were to be extended with vector search, lack of ready-made createIndex code risks authors writing the wrong Mongo-style createIndex and failing to create the index on DocumentDB. The current sample does not use vectors, so this gap did not break the build, but it is a common authoring pitfall.
doc_gaps.proposed_content:
Title: 'Create a vector index in Node.js (copy/paste)'
Outline:
- Short Node.js snippet using db.command({ createIndexes: '<coll>', indexes: [...] }) with cosmosSearchOptions.kind: 'vector-hnsw' (or 'vector-ivf' / 'vector-diskann')
- Example parameter values for small/medium/large datasets and recommended dims/metric
- Example query showing $search usage and reading scores
Priority: medium

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A short, prominent statement on public pages clarifying that Azure DocumentDB (vCore Mongo-compatible clusters) is billed by compute tier (vCores) + storage and is not the RU-based Cosmos DB offering.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Product quickstarts, pricing pages and the agent skills; discovery logs show models and authors conflate RU guidance with DocumentDB vCore behavior.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Builders could pick incorrect scaling/monitoring semantics or example code that mentions RU/s. This build used a live vCore cluster and did not rely on RU guidance, but confusion in docs will cause authoring mistakes in other samples.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short 'Billing & capacity model' note on the Azure DocumentDB landing/quickstart pages: clearly state 'Azure DocumentDB (vCore) — billed by compute tier and storage; not RU/s'. Add a tiny table comparing vCore DocumentDB vs RU-based Cosmos DB to prevent conflation.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A small verification script or README step that runs explain('executionStats') against the sample's critical queries and explains how to interpret IXSCAN vs COLLSCAN output.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Indexing and explain pages on Microsoft Learn and documentdb skills; guidance exists but no repository-level example that authors can run in a sample.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder created appropriate indexes but did not run explain() as part of seed/verification. A discoverability gap means authors may forget this verification step.
doc_gaps.proposed_content:
Title: 'Verify indexes with explain() (sample script)'
Outline:
- Node script example that calls collection.find(query).explain('executionStats') and prints key parts
- README snippet describing how to read executionStats and what to change if COLLSCAN appears
Priority: medium
